title: Gandhian Thought
author: Akash Naik
text:
I was fierce when I was young,
I would lose my temper over little things.
I was strongly built, too,
but words did not come easily to me.

Whenever I quarrelled,
I would run out of words;
my fist would rise to the seventh heaven,
my tongue would falter,
and my hands would take over.

Thus, in the innocence of youth,
violence would happen.

With age came understanding;
struggles came, and with them,
my nature began to change.
Yet anger remained—
only its intensity diminished.

Reading, reflection and contemplation grew.
I read Gandhi,
and violence began to fade.
I embraced the idea of non-violence.

For a while,
violence and non-violence
walked side by side.

Then age entered its forest,
and the mind became still water.
I turned away from conflict;
non-violence returned,
again and again.

And yet—
I am still
trying to understand
Gandhian thought.
